title: Mismatch and Coordinate-Correction Rejection
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $w,w_0:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and choose a coordinate $i$. Suppose that, for a uniformly random $y\in\mathbb F_2^n$, the local correction $f(e_i+y)f(y)$ equals the sign encoded by $w_0(i)$ with probability at least $1/2$. Then the probability that the same correction fails to equal the sign encoded by $w(i)$ is at least $1/2$ if $w(i)\ne w_0(i)$; if they agree, the claimed lower bound is zero.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on $\mathbb F_2^n$
$w$ and $w_0$ are Boolean strings of length $n$
The correction probability for $w_0(i)$ is at least $1/2$
